pairs.question: Paete, quid aetatem numeras? quid cara natanti mater in ore tibist?
pairs.derivation: Apostrophe to the drowned Paetus: the poet poses rhetorical questions (quid aetatem numeras / quid cara mater in ore) and answers them himself with the terse maxim 'non habet unda deos' ('the wave has no gods'). Window ends at the first full stop; what follows (et mater non iusta...) turns from answering to elaborating Paetus's plight. No framing word to strip; only terminal capitalization normalized.

pairs.question: Quidnam visissent mane Camenae, ante meum stantes sole rubente torum?
pairs.answer: Natalis nostrae signum misere puellae et manibus faustos ter crepuere sonos.
pairs.derivation: Indirect question introduced by the framing verb 'Mirabar' ('I was wondering why...'), which is dropped as narration of the asking; the remaining words (quidnam visissent... torum) are the author's, in source order, presented as a direct question. The poet answers himself: the Muses came to bring the sign of his girl's birthday. Window ends at the first full stop (line 435); what follows (transeat hic sine nube dies...) is the birthday wish, no longer answering. First word capitalized and terminal punctuation normalized.

pairs.question: Unde avidis nox sit pretiosa puellis, et Venere exhaustae damna querantur opes?
pairs.answer: Certa quidem tantis causa et manifesta ruinis: luxuriae nimium libera facta viast.
pairs.derivation: Indirect question introduced by the framing verb 'Quaeritis' ('you ask why...'), dropped as narration of the asking; the dependent clause (unde avidis nox sit pretiosa... querantur opes) is the author's own words in source order, presented as the direct question. The poet answers himself: 'certa quidem... causa... luxuriae nimium libera facta viast'. The colon after 'ruinis' is internal to the answering sentence (not a full stop), so the window runs to the first full stop after 'viast'. First word capitalized; terminal punctuation normalized.
